This game took me about 3.5 hours to complete on my first playthrough (there are alternate endings available). I tried to read every bit of text and watch every video / photo involved. This game does disappoint as a horror game, but as a mystery thriller, it is excellent. 

This is not a mixed or alternate reality game where you search the web for answers or give your e-mail. The experience is pretty linear, although you can make different choices, the experience goes pretty much through the same set of main events (except for the endings which can vary). You will be looking through videos, photos, Jabbr (facebook), Spark (Tinder), the web (in-game only browser), phone numbers, and e-mails. You simply have to find the relevant information to unlock passcodes or find connections to progress the story. 

You will also have dialogue choices. Some of those choices can have an impact on the story, for example, having more trust with that person and thus giving you a different ending. The story starts out very strong when it is a mystery about what happened to the missing woman, Anna. Even the creepy stuff is exciting at first when you see the distorted videos and the atmosphere leaves things to the imagination. The dialogue between characters is well-written. 

Unfortunately, when you find out the mystery then the horror elements become more silly than scary. I actually just started to troll everybody, trying to get the worst possible ending. There was some real tension at the start and middle of this game, but towards the end, I really didn't feel any connection to any of the characters or "the danger" involved.

That's a shame because this is a very polished experience. The actors all did a nice job overall (sure some of the acting could have been better, but it's better than what is in most games). The mystery sequences where you're sleuthing and trying to find the truth all work extremely well. It's just too bad it ends in a whimper instead of a bang.

Went into this completely blind and found it to be a decent game with a slightly above average horror storyline. There are a lot of jump-scare tactics in this visual novel/detective game, many of them unnecessary and overused. The FMVs were done pretty well and the interface is intuitive. The game encourages you to play it again to get different outcomes, but when the first playthrough is over 3 hours I can't be bothered to play a linear story and make sure that I selected certain dialogue options to get all endings/100% achievements.

One thing that I absolutely found hilarious was Greg's voice acting. It's so campy and over-the-top that the first time I heard it I couldn't help but bust out laughing. I'm sure that when he recorded it he had to be clear and precise with his lines, but holy crap it just sounds like a Dragonball Z character powering up for a fight.

I recommend this only because what it does well, it does it *really* well (atmosphere, NPC dialogue, FMV, interface). For the other stuff, it's borderline 80's slasher B-movie status trying to take itself a bit too seriously. There seemed to be some missed opportunities here and gaping plot holes, but I would play another game very similar to this by the same developer with a few new tricks.

Overall, mostly worth your time. Might play Simulacra 2 when I get the chance.

I am generally biased to be forgiving of FMV interactive movies, so of course I've played others like Her Story, #WarGames, The Bunker, Late Shift, and The Shapeshifting Detective.  Like those games, this game is relatively short on total content, with moments of good acting and then...well, near-miss moments that make you cringe.  Also, these games tend to have multiple achievements and scenes that you can't get in one playthrough, which is a way of extending the replay value, but I seldom feel particularly inclined to watch the repeated parts over and over again.

This game is unique due to the phone interface and the clever design that it took to make that work.  You feel like it really could be you deciding what to do in this situation, but then sometimes you're reminded how you can't actually do anything like answer a phone call.  So when it works, it's great, but it has built-in limitations to just how far the concept can go.  I commend them for the creepy story.  I wish the really uneven voice acting hadn't pulled me out of it from time to time.  At least Anna (whose phone you've found) is done consistently well.

Your first full playthrough will take 3-4 hours depending on how much you read, and subsequent plays should take you a bit less.  Alternate achievements, videos, conversations, and endings are basically earned by the responses you choose, like who to be nice to, who to scold, and who to trust.  The downside of that is like the decisions in Telltale games, especially The Walking Dead: you'll have to replay with lots of choices that you'd never make in real life if you want to see the other paths.  In that regard, replays are more like gaming the game and less like experiencing the story.  But overall, that's a complaint that's bound to be true of every choose-your-own-adventure game you can find.  So you know what you're getting.  If you like that, and you have a tolerance for FMV games, this one is certainly worth $5.

A decent puzzle type game. While there are the occasional mild jump scares and something strange going on, it didn't really give me a horror or suspense vibe.

Pros:
- I generally stay away from FMV games, but the actresses & voice actors are actually pretty good
- The puzzle difficulty is OK for the most part
- Several other easter eggs and hidden puzzles if you want an extra challenge
- Has a mode for replaying to make text speed up instead of being at a realistic speed

Cons:
- Lacking in horror, and didn't feel that suspenseful
- Texts and responses when texting are often not quite right - grammatically wrong or just don't completely make sense. It could have used some more polish.
- Setting aside the fact that you're going through a stranger's phone instead of giving it to the police/family/etc, there are still things you have to do to progress the story that I would never think to do IRL
- While you frequently have different options for responses to messages, responses to what you say are frequently reused, giving the illusion of more choice than you really have. Good for role playing, but noticeable when replaying
- Has mutually exclusive achievements and different endings, but lacks replayability. Yes you can choose different dialogue option that can influence people differently, but the puzzles and their solutions are still the same.
- I wasn't a big fan of the ending. It didn't make much sense and wasn't really explained. That may have been saved for the second game though.

Verdict: 7/10

Very atmospheric and innovative horror game about hacking a girls phone to look through her chats and pics. She's also missing so you're somehow trying to find out where she is by cooperating with her ex-boyfriend and the meme guy she was chatting with on Tinder.

It feels very realistic most of the time, especially the puzzles are very logical and make sense so this is finally an adventure game where rational thought will actually bring you forward. The game can also be really creepy but its one of those horror games where the setup is really good and mysterious but the resolution is not satisfying (To me the explanation for everything that happened seemed just extremely wacky and bizarre and not in a good way).

Sometimes it was a bit like a social media drama simulator but I guess that was to make the scary parts more effective when they suddenly happen.
